analysis:
Reviewed the head-side text of MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift lines 1-1017. The visible changes add Flint support: line 327 now also checks rawFlintControls.invalid via the read-only resident lookup (the existing pattern); line 449 calls FlintRequestPolicy.validate; line 901 builds answerStopFilter from a FlintAnswerStopConstraint; line 934 sets engineStopStrings: modelType != "flint"; and lines 998-1001 pass answerStopFilter and withholdReasoning into makeDeadlineCheckedEventStream. Later hunks (1114-1519) are outside the supplied units, and the patch excerpt is truncated, so they were not examined.

Security-relevant observations:
- The new validation paths release the reservation via releaseBox.fire() on throw, as the existing code does. I found no reservation leak in the visible code.
- The Flint control validation at 327 uses the same read-only lookup. It does not load models and does not infer the type from the requested name. It runs before acquisition, so the pre-acquire invalid-control check cannot trigger a cold load.
- Disabling engine-side stop strings for Flint moves stop matching into the stream filter. This is a correctness and confidentiality-adjacent behavior: if the filter is bypassed or buggy, a stop string might not truncate output. I found no direct data-exposure path in the visible code.
- withholdReasoning for Flint suppresses reasoning output. Its enforcement lives in the event stream builder and FlintRequestPolicy, which are not supplied. Reasoning leakage to the consumer is therefore unverified.
- Prefix-cache scope handling is unchanged: cacheScope, cacheEnabled and donationDemand are still passed to the bridge, so T-041 is not affected by the visible diff.

Remaining integration questions: the implementations of FlintAnswerStopConstraint, FlintRequestPolicy, rawFlintControls and makeDeadlineCheckedEventStream; the later changed hunks in this file; and whether Flint prompts or reasoning could be logged in telemetry.
